import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file path
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_16/training_0.csv"
    # Output file path
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_16/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load source table with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
    df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

    # According to the target schema: ['CUSTOMERNAME': string, 'ORDERNUMBER': integer]
    # Extract only these two columns from source0
    # Ensure ORDERNUMBER is integer type (may need to convert)
    # CUSTOMERNAME is string, but pandas will handle it as object/string by default

    # Drop rows where CUSTOMERNAME or ORDERNUMBER is missing (NaN)
    df_filtered = df_source0[['CUSTOMERNAME', 'ORDERNUMBER']].dropna(subset=['CUSTOMERNAME', 'ORDERNUMBER'])

    # Convert ORDERNUMBER to integer (some may be float due to CSV reading)

    # Reset index to default integer index

    # Save the transformed dataframe to the output CSV file
    df_filtered.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import pandas as pd

# Read source table with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_16/training_0.csv", index_col=0)

# Select only relevant columns CUSTOMERNAME and ORDERNUMBER
df = source1[['CUSTOMERNAME', 'ORDERNUMBER']]

# Remove rows with missing CUSTOMERNAME or ORDERNUMBER
df = df.dropna(subset=['CUSTOMERNAME', 'ORDERNUMBER'])

# Convert ORDERNUMBER to integer (if not already)
df['ORDERNUMBER'] = df['ORDERNUMBER'].astype(int)

# Group by CUSTOMERNAME and aggregate ORDERNUMBER by min to enforce uniqueness
result = df.groupby('CUSTOMERNAME', as_index=False).agg({'ORDERNUMBER': 'min'})

# Write output with exact target schema column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_16/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
